projects.name: DocVault

screenshot.alt: DocVault shows the amount due, due date and billing period extracted from a sample electricity bill.
screenshot.caption: DocVault’s bill review screen with a synthetic electricity bill.

projects.summary: Digitise manuals, warranties and guides, then find the information you need with keyword and meaning-based search.
projects.status: Local web and backend MVP implemented
projects.purpose: DocVault is my final-year project: a document management app for digitising physical manuals, warranties and guides and finding information within them. It connects document storage and text extraction with search and document-grounded Q&A.
projects.approach: A React and TypeScript client connects to a FastAPI backend. PostgreSQL full-text search and pgvector provide keyword and semantic retrieval in the same database. Redis and an ARQ worker handle document processing in the background, with an inline fallback when the queue is unavailable.
projects.decision: Combining relational data and both search methods in one database keeps the architecture simpler. Background processing lets uploads return while text extraction and indexing continue.
projects.evidenceText: The repository’s current-state report documents the local runtime, automated checks and a bill-review rehearsal. It also identifies the remaining evaluation and deployment work.
projects.limitations: Formal evaluation, physical-device validation and evidence of a live AWS deployment remain in progress. Generated AI answers were not verified in the documented smoke run because no live answer-provider key was active.

projects.name: VibeCam

screenshot.alt: VibeCam shows an imported photo and camera looks in the photo editor.
screenshot.caption: VibeCam’s photo editor in the web preview, using a sample photo.

projects.summary: An offline pocket-camera simulator with six compact-camera-inspired looks for photos and short videos. Import, compare and restyle while keeping the original.
projects.status: In development · Physical iPhone testing pending
projects.purpose: VibeCam is an iPhone camera app in development, focused on offline photo and short-video looks. Users can capture or import a photo, compare different looks and preview adjustments before applying an edit.
projects.approach: The Expo, React Native and TypeScript app uses local photo rendering and a custom iPhone module for short video export. Film Roll retains originals and applied edits, so users can restyle media without compounding an earlier edit. Cloud features are disabled by default for the first release.
projects.decision: Keeping the original separate from the edit lets people change their mind. The same committed media is used for preview, saving and sharing, helping the output stay consistent with the applied edit.
projects.evidenceText: The release-readiness document records development tests, rendering checks and browser walkthroughs. It also provides a physical iPhone walkthrough for capture, audio, export, storage and permissions.
projects.limitations: Physical iPhone validation remains before release. The six looks are camera-inspired interpretations, rather than measured matches to camera hardware. The app is not presented as an App Store release.

projects.name: Exoplanet AI Hunter

screenshot.alt: The Exoplanet AI Hunter home screen introduces the classifier and shows a button to start classification.
screenshot.caption: Exoplanet AI Hunter’s web app for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

projects.summary: A machine-learning classification project using Kepler, K2 and TESS observations to support exoplanet follow-up prioritisation.
projects.purpose: Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025, Exoplanet AI Hunter brings machine learning and a web interface together to classify transit observations for follow-up prioritisation.
projects.approach: A Random Forest model works with astronomical observation parameters. A Flask interface exposes the classification workflow, while Python, pandas and scikit-learn support data processing and modelling. The repository uses observation data from NASA’s Kepler, K2 and TESS missions.
projects.decision: Presenting the model through a web interface makes its observation inputs and classification output easier to explore than a standalone training script.
projects.evidenceText: The public repository contains the application, data-processing and model-training code, setup instructions and tests.
projects.limitations: This is a classification project. A model’s classification does not establish that a new planet has been discovered or independently confirmed.

projects.name: CourseXcel

screenshot.alt: CourseXcel’s admin dashboard shows charts for subject assignments and lecturer claims.
screenshot.caption: CourseXcel’s reporting dashboard with fictional departments and lecturer records.

projects.summary: Subject assignment, lecturer claims and departmental reporting in one application, with distinct permissions and workflows for each role.
projects.purpose: As Team Leader, I worked on CourseXcel from September to December 2024. The application supports course administration, subject assignments, part-time lecturers and monthly claims, with different workflows for administrators, programme officers and lecturers.
projects.approach: The web application uses Python, Flask, JavaScript and MySQL. It automates course-structure conversion and cost calculations alongside subject assignments, lecturer claims and departmental reports. Role-based permissions keep each workflow aligned with the user’s responsibilities.
projects.decision: Separating the workflows by role keeps each user’s actions and information aligned with their responsibilities. The project shows my interest in practical business software alongside AI applications.
projects.evidenceText: The public repository describes the role-based workflows and contains the application source. My CV records my Team Leader role and the project’s work on course-structure conversion and workflow automation.
projects.limitations: The source documents the application’s functionality. I would use a repeatable evaluation with a defined dataset to establish comparable accuracy and time-saving results before extending the system.

projects.name: F1 Strategy Visualisation

screenshot.alt: The F1 Strategy Visualisation dashboard compares tyre stints for six drivers at the Austrian Grand Prix.
screenshot.caption: Tyre strategy view in the interactive Austrian Grand Prix dashboard.

projects.summary: Exploring race pace, tyre age and pit-stop context through an interactive story. I am Head Developer in the group project.
projects.status: Story prototype · Audience feedback in progress
projects.purpose: A group data visualisation project for F1 fans, initially studying the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix. It explores race pace, tyre age and pit-stop context. The team workflow names me as Head Developer.
projects.approach: The preparation pipeline retains selected source laps and marks eligibility for normal-racing pace comparisons. A Streamlit story prototype combines pace context, matched race-window comparisons, stint accounting and pit/VSC exploration.
projects.decision: Keeping the recorded laps and their eligibility flags helps make the basis of comparisons visible. Race-window and stint context matter when interpreting differences in lap time.
projects.evidenceText: The repository includes the audience brief, data audit, preparation pipeline and story prototype, together with documentation of the comparisons and their limits.
projects.limitations: Audience feedback and the final story remain in progress. Fuel load, traffic and conditions also affect lap times; the data cannot isolate causal tyre degradation or establish an optimal race strategy.

Automated the Trouble Report data pipeline, syncing live Jira data through SharePoint into Power BI dashboards to eliminate manual reporting and provide real-time visibility.
Developed an OCR-based sticker extraction system with a self-trained AI model, improving data processing accuracy by 35% and reducing manual validation time by 50%.
Achieved 98% text-extraction accuracy and 94% LLM response accuracy by integrating PaddleOCR and Amazon Bedrock pipelines using Claude and Qwen to process PDF documents.
Automated AXI machine-data retrieval and workflow updates using Python scripts, reducing manual labour time by 75%.
